ppi_focus: Compression and leakdown test, plus oil condition and any signs of consumption
ECU scan for tune or reflash status, readiness monitors and stored codes; confirm CARB compliance of any engine parts
Rear structure behind the aftermarket trunk lid: trunk floor, rear panel and tail-light pockets for repair or paint evidence; paint-meter readings
Trunk-lid wiring for the third brake light and camera/lock; check function and sound mounting of the wing and struts
Clutch engagement point, slip under load, throwout-bearing noise and synchro feel in 2nd and 3rd
Suspension: stock versus aftermarket parts, bushings, alignment and inner-edge tire wear that would indicate track use
Tire date codes and matching set; brake pad and rotor condition
Underside for scrapes, impact damage or corrosion from any out-of-state history
Valve-cover and timing-cover seepage and the fuel-pump whine typical of the FA20; check open recalls by VIN
what_would_change_verdict: Up: a clean Carfax PDF, an untuned and never-tracked engine confirmed at PPI, and a clean scan with good compression.
Up: the price negotiated toward the comps (about $16,500-$17,500) with the original trunk lid included or the history of the swap explained.
Down: evidence of rear-end accident repair behind the trunk swap, a tuned ECU or non-CARB parts, or track-use signs such as oil consumption or worn inner tire edges.
Down: the seller refuses an independent PPI or will not give an out-the-door figure.
evidence.mission_note: A manual, naturally aspirated, easily resold BRZ local to Carmel fits the enthusiast-bridge brief well as a secondary candidate. The cosmetic modifications and the above-comp asking price are what need answering.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes a 2016 BRZ Limited with a 6-speed manual (visible in the photo), 51,610 claimed miles, and claimed one-owner, clean-title status with a Carfax referenced but not captured. The photos show it on what appears to be a Toyota dealer lot in Salinas, contrary to the tracker's 'Private' tag. They also show an aftermarket carbon-look trunk lid with a large wing and exposed wiring, which is a sign of an enthusiast owner and possibly of rear repair. The windshield sticker reads $18,999 against the $19,999 ask; both sit above the $16,400 sale of a lower-mileage 2017 Limited. Neither applicable recall concerns this model year. Track history, tune status, clutch condition, tires and service records are all unestablished. The late-series California plate hints at a recent California registration, which the Carfax should explain.
evidence.next_action: Get the VIN and Carfax PDF and confirm the out-the-door price, then book a test drive and independent PPI in Salinas. The PPI should cover compression/leakdown, an ECU scan and an inspection of the rear structure under the aftermarket trunk lid.
